problem.title: Team Points Standings from Head-to-Head Matches
problem.prompt: A fitness challenge app tracks team-versus-team workout competitions. Each match is recorded as one row with both teams and their scores. The `workout_matches` table has columns `match_id`, `home_team_id`, `away_team_id`, `home_score`, and `away_score`, representing the number of completed workouts each team achieved during the match period. Calculate each team's total points using standard scoring: a team earns 3 points for a win (higher score than opponent), 1 point for a draw (equal scores), and 0 points for a loss. Report every team in the `teams` table, even if they have not participated in any matches yet (show 0 points and 0 matches for those teams). Output columns: `team_name`, `matches_played`, `total_points`. Order the results by `total_points` descending, then by `team_name` ascending.
problem.schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE teams (team_id INT PRIMARY KEY, team_name VARCHAR(100)); CREATE TABLE workout_matches (match_id INT PRIMARY KEY, home_team_id INT, away_team_id INT, home_score INT, away_score INT);
problem.example_input_data: INSERT INTO teams (team_id, team_name) VALUES (1, 'Alpha Lifters'), (2, 'Beta Runners'), (3, 'Gamma Cyclists'), (4, 'Delta Yogis'); INSERT INTO workout_matches (match_id, home_team_id, away_team_id, home_score, away_score) VALUES (101, 1, 2, 12, 8), (102, 2, 3, 10, 10), (103, 3, 1, 7, 9), (104, 1, 3, 15, 15), (105, 2, 1, 6, 11);

composite_moves: unpivot the two sides of each match via UNION ALL, producing one row per (team, own_score, opponent_score)
score each unpivoted row: CASE WHEN own_score > opp_score THEN 3 WHEN own_score = opp_score THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
GROUP BY team_id aggregating SUM(points) and COUNT(*) as matches_played
LEFT JOIN from teams dimension to the aggregated results, COALESCE metrics to 0 for teams with no matches
ORDER BY total_points DESC, team_name ASC

hints: Each match row contains two teams; you need to extract each team's perspective separately so you can count all their matches.

Use UNION ALL to split each match into two rows: one for the home team (with home_score as their score and away_score as opponent) and one for the away team (reversed). Then apply the point-scoring rule to each row.

After unpivoting, use CASE to assign points: 3 if own_score > opponent_score, 1 if equal, 0 otherwise. Then GROUP BY team_id, SUM the points and COUNT the matches. Finally, LEFT JOIN from the teams table so every team appears, using COALESCE to default missing aggregates to 0.
problem.answer_key:
WITH team_results AS (
  SELECT
    home_team_id AS team_id,
    home_score AS own_score,
    away_score AS opp_score
  FROM workout_matches
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    away_team_id AS team_id,
    away_score AS own_score,
    home_score AS opp_score
  FROM workout_matches
),
team_points AS (
  SELECT
    team_id,
    COUNT(*) AS matches_played,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN own_score > opp_score THEN 3
        WHEN own_score = opp_score THEN 1
        ELSE 0
      END
    ) AS total_points
  FROM team_results
  GROUP BY team_id
)
SELECT
  t.team_name,
  COALESCE(tp.matches_played, 0)::TEXT AS matches_played,
  COALESCE(tp.total_points, 0)::TEXT AS total_points
FROM teams t
LEFT JOIN team_points tp ON t.team_id = tp.team_id
ORDER BY COALESCE(tp.total_points, 0) DESC, t.team_name ASC;

_meta.scenario: a fitness app tracking workout completion and active days per week

user_solution:
/*
1. score and pivot
2. group by

*/

WITH base AS (
    SELECT
        w.match_id::int,
        t.team_id,
        t.team_name,
        CASE 
            WHEN w.home_score > w.away_score THEN 3
            WHEN w.home_score = w.away_score THEN 1
            WHEN w.home_score < w.away_score THEN 0
        END AS team_scores
    FROM teams AS t
    LEFT JOIN workout_matches AS w
    ON t.team_id = w.home_team_id

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        w.match_id::int,
        t.team_id,
        t.team_name,
        CASE 
            WHEN w.home_score < w.away_score THEN 3
            WHEN w.home_score = w.away_score THEN 1
            WHEN w.home_score > w.away_score THEN 0
        END AS team_scores
    FROM teams AS t
    LEFT JOIN workout_matches AS w
    ON t.team_id = w.away_team_id

)
SELECT
    b.team_name,
    COALESCE(COUNT(b.match_id),0) AS matches_played,
    COALESCE(SUM(b.team_scores),0) AS total_points
FROM base AS b
GROUP BY b.team_name
ORDER BY total_points DESC, team_name;
